Breakdown.Freq.X.text: The stored Fourier field represents one homogeneous derivative of velocity, rather than velocity itself.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinX.text: The code defines the interaction through a trilinear pairing against a smoothed test, while the prose first writes it as a projected physical nonlinearity.

Breakdown.Freq.bilinCompact_holds.text: The declaration retains only the dense-subspace version needed by the abstract framework.

Breakdown.Freq.mild_holds.text: The code proves a Fourier-space test-density route, while the printed paper invokes Dubois.

Breakdown.orbitNorm.text: The proof excludes small slices by comparison with a bounded small-data solution, instead of taking a positive minimum over a period.

Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile.text: The extra bounds are assumptions in this definition. The manuscript supplies their analytic derivation from the paper profile.

Breakdown.monodromy.text: The source subdivides a similarity period until each interval operator has norm at most one quarter. The paper defines one full-period Volterra operator; uniqueness identifies the resulting period maps.

Breakdown.Spectral.exists_dichotomy.text: Inverse decay is expressed as a lower bound for forward powers on the finite-dimensional range, plus surjectivity. This avoids naming an inverse in the statement.

Breakdown.orbitSeq.text: The source sequence is normalized by the decay factor. The continuous-source recurrence must first be derived for v minus g.

Breakdown.exists_section.text: The returned map lifts the exceptional component into compact data. Its image can have a stable component, which remains in the forward recurrence.

Breakdown.periodicInverse.text: The input is a bounded sequence of short-interval functions. Proposition 5.3 gives the corresponding continuous weighted formulation separately.

Breakdown.contraction.text: The exported theorem bounds the correction but does not retain its membership in the exceptional range. The proof takes that correction from the first component of the right inverse.

Breakdown.TransferHolds.text: The export retains dense-data existence and rescaled convergence. The paper also states a correction for every sufficiently nearby datum in one fixed finite-dimensional space.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose.text: The source keeps a fixed cutoff near the centre of a unit torus and lets the blow-up scale shrink. The rewrite uses a large cutoff radius before the later change of scale.

Breakdown.Periodic.transplantNorm.text: The extra mass term comes from the formal inhomogeneous H1 norm. The scaled term vanishes in the small-time limit.

Breakdown.Periodic.transplantField.text: The formal copy is placed at the centre of the unit cube. The paper places its core at the origin; a translation changes the location.

Breakdown.Periodic.heatDivFreeComparison.text: The formal proof separates short times from the comparison window. The revised paper uses an Oseen-kernel estimate uniform for every positive time.

Breakdown.Periodic.shellInverseTransfer.text: The source uses abstract Banach spaces and maps: Rr is the restriction D, Sop is the reduced operator, and RS is its right inverse. The selected lines also show the max-product norm bound; identifying the component spaces with continuous weighted spaces is a separate analytic step.

Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup.text: This definition retains a smooth periodic datum and an unbounded mild Fourier trajectory. The printed rates and local physical convergence are additional clauses.

Breakdown.Periodic.movingFrameReduction.text: A periodic velocity can have an affine pressure term. The time-dependent frame removes that term and is chosen to preserve the datum.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.GradSixDecay.cut.text: These declarations construct the cutoff. They do not alone prove completion for every distributional-gradient field in the surrounding paragraph.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.NiceDense.smooth.text: The smoothing helper assumes annular support. The preceding truncation and the subsequent convergence argument remain separate steps.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.NiceDense.symFie.text: The source uses complex Fourier symbols for real physical fields.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.NiceDense.norm_p.text: The projection smoothness premise excludes a neighborhood of zero; the averaging estimate assumes the target has the reality symmetry.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.NiceApprox.symbo.text: This link identifies each approximating field. The displayed sequence convergence also uses the preceding approximation estimates and the embedding interfaces.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.NiceApprox.cutof.text: cutoff_tendsto also controls the gradient of the negative Laplacian error, which is stronger than the gradient convergence used here.
The source makes an individual epsilon choice; applying it successively to a sequence is the prose organization of those choices.

Breakdown.Freq.longitudinal.text: This identifies the pointwise Fourier projection formula. Projection of the full encoded real Fourier space also imposes reality symmetry.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.NiceDense.div_pr.text: This is the Fourier algebra that enforces the solenoidal constraint; the realization of the heat output as a physical field is a separate bridge.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.BilinExists.bili.text: The source defines the interaction by its dual pairings and proves existence under TrilinearBound and PhiBounds. The physical multiplier formula is a separate identification.

Breakdown.Freq.BilinSpec.text: The sentence describes the encoding: its defining expression does not take a pointwise Fourier transform of an arbitrary nonlinear product.

Breakdown.compactPiece_of.text: The linked lines use Mathlib closedness. The following diagonal-subsequence explanation is the reading text proof of that general fact.

Breakdown.Freq.Internal.GradSixDecay.mem.text: The linked clause is the integrability step; membership in the encoded space also uses the embedding construction.

Breakdown.HeatBilinear.HasCompactKernel.text: The Fourier compactness proof uses Fourier restriction, Arzela-Ascoli, and tail bounds; the earlier physical-space Rellich proof is a different route.

Breakdown.Periodic.Cutoff.Internal.hasFD.text: These helpers concern the spatial parameter. They do not by themselves state joint smoothness in the extra physical-time parameter of the surrounding construction.

Breakdown.Periodic.homotopyCurl.text: The declaration is a spatial identity for any center x0; it is applied to each time slice in the reading text.
